name: Pragma BioSync Underlayer Mark II
description: A second-skin compression shirt and legging set in deep slate blue with subtle silver biometric-trace lines running along major vascular pathways — decorative only from the outside, but each line conceals a sensor filament. The Mark II reads heart rate, blood oxygenation, cortisol levels, hydration, and skin galvanic response, feeding data continuously to a paired BCI or wristmount. Fabric is smooth matte elastane-synthetic with just enough compression to feel intentional without being medical. Common among Tier 3 desk workers trying to optimize.
functionality: Continuous passive biometric monitoring synced to BCI or companion app; alerts for stress spikes, dehydration, and cardiac irregularities. Light compression aids circulation during sedentary work. Port loop at the nape routes data without external cabling.
what_it_says: You're optimizing yourself the way you optimize a spreadsheet — methodically, slightly anxiously.
manufacturer: Pragma Systems — Tier 3 wellness corponation label
story_hooks: The Mark II's data feed is stored server-side by Pragma — a leaked document suggests that data is being sold to insurance underwriters.
A wearer's cortisol log shows they were in extreme distress at the exact time they claim they were home asleep.
Someone has been spoofing healthy biometric readings through a hardware mod — and they're about to walk into a mandatory corporate wellness screening.
